bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion indicates that Rumble is gaining scale across its video and AI infrastructure activities. If this growth persists, greater utilization of its platform and infrastructure assets can improve operating leverage, broaden customer relationships, and support stronger future earnings capacity.

The AI infrastructure business has quickly become Rumble’s primary growth engine and is already producing substantial adjusted EBITDA. High GPU utilization and reported profitability provide evidence of demand, asset productivity, and a potentially durable infrastructure-led earnings model.

A sustained positive gross margin in the video segment would reduce the burden that historically unprofitable media operations place on the wider company. Combined with the cost reset and automation strategy, this could create a more disciplined platform capable of supporting creator growth.

bear.b: Severe ongoing losses show that improved revenue and gross margin have not yet translated into sustainable profitability. Continued negative earnings can erode equity value, require additional financing, and limit management’s ability to reinvest while the company scales its infrastructure and media businesses.

Substantial operating and free cash flow deficits mean Rumble is not yet self-funding its growth. Persistent cash consumption increases dependence on liquidity, financing, or customer prepayments and could constrain expansion if infrastructure investment and operating losses remain elevated over coming quarters.

bear.t: AI Expansion and Financing Execution Risk
bear.b: Rumble’s infrastructure opportunity depends on financing and timely project execution, yet management describes a difficult capital environment and expects some capacity to slip beyond 2027. Delays could defer revenue growth, prolong investment needs, and reduce the near-term payoff from its AI strategy.
